title: DARPA CALO → Siri
summary: CALO (Cognitive Assistant that Learns and Organizes) was SRI International's component of DARPA's Personalized Assistant that Learns (PAL) program, a five-year AI effort begun in 2003 that SRI says involved more than 300 researchers from 22 institutions. In 2007 SRI spun off Siri, Inc. to bring assistant technology from that work to consumers; the startup raised venture capital from Menlo Ventures and Morgenthaler Ventures and was acquired by Apple in April 2010. DARPA and SRI both describe Siri as an outcome of PAL/CALO, and Siri's founding team included SRI's CALO chief architect and an SRI entrepreneur-in-residence. Sources differ on when CALO itself ended (2007 or 2008), and DARPA still listed PAL as an active program in 2011.

links.claim: DARPA's own program history says PAL advances in voice interaction on handheld devices led to the 2007 launch of Siri Inc., later acquired by Apple, which integrated the 'Siri/PAL technology' into its mobile operating system.

SRI International states that the Siri technology was developed through the SRI-led CALO project within DARPA's PAL program, and that SRI spun off Siri, Inc. in 2007 to bring that technology to consumers. Terms of any license or equity arrangement were not found in public sources.

Contemporaneous coverage reported that Siri was spun out of SRI to commercialize the results of the SRI-led CALO project, and that CALO was the source of Siri's core technology for understanding, classifying and responding to user requests.

claims.claim: Siri was a DARPA project / the Pentagon built Siri.
claims.explanation: The underlying research came from CALO, SRI's part of DARPA's PAL program, and DARPA itself credits PAL with leading to Siri Inc. But Siri Inc. was a separate venture-backed startup founded in 2007 that turned the research into a consumer product; DARPA's PAL program was aimed at military command staffs, and DARPA still described PAL as an active military program in 2011.

claims.claim: DARPA spent $150 million (or $200 million) developing Siri.
claims.explanation: SRI's $150 million figure describes the whole five-year CALO/PAL effort involving more than 300 researchers at 22 institutions, of which Siri was one later commercial outcome; it was not a budget for Siri. Siri, Inc. itself raised $24 million in private financing. The $200 million figure appears in press coverage but was not found in DARPA or SRI records.
